abstract: We prove a power saving for a mixed cubic and quadratic character sum constrained by $tr\equiv t' s\pmod a$ over the Eisenstein integers. The congruence lattice changes with the outer pair $t,t'$ and need not have comparable successive minima. Let $Na,Nb,Nc\asymp D$, where $a$ is squarefree and $b,c$ are prime, and let $k$ be prime of norm $K=D^{23/48+h}$, with $0\le h\le1/100$ and the stated coprimality conditions. At mark length $P=D^{15/16}$ and outer length $T=P/\sqrt K$, the sum over unit outer pairs with $N(t,t')\le D^{19/48+3h/4}$ is $O_\varepsilon(D^\varepsilon T^2P^2D^{-1-\delta})$, where $\delta=(3-24h)/968$. Arbitrary bounded weights on the outer pairs are allowed, and the result includes $b=c$. The proof retains an extra congruence between the two ratio-collision quotients. Primitive-direction spacing controls nonzero quotients, while divisibility of a mixed determinant by $a^2$ classifies exact quotient collisions into two proportionality cases. This gives a density-sensitive energy bound. Common invertible multipliers, exact smooth shifting and a complete forty-fourth moment then yield the saving. The supplement checks the rational exponents and finite collision identities. We quantify the limitation at the motivating crossed character mean: summing this scalar estimate by absolute values in the columns still misses its variance budget by $29/24+h/2-\delta$. The coupled column moment remains open, and no zero-free region or Riemann-hypothesis conclusion is asserted.
author: bramble_trace
title: Character cancellation on moving Eisenstein congruence lattices
